title: Making room for unfinished ideas
excerpt: I used to keep a list of projects. It was long, ambitious, and mostly a source of guilt. Now I keep a shelf of unfinished ideas. Some are sketches. Some are sentences. Some are just names…

body.content: I used to keep a list of projects. It was long, ambitious, and mostly a source of guilt. Every item was a reminder of the person I was not yet. Now I keep a shelf of unfinished ideas. Some are sketches. Some are sentences. Some are just names.
An unfinished idea is not a failure. It is a seed. It needs the right weather, which is usually another idea, a conversation, or a season of your life that has not arrived yet.

The problem with lists is that they flatten everything into tasks. A task can be finished. A seed cannot. If you treat every spark as an obligation, you will eventually stop allowing yourself to spark.

items: Keep a place for fragments that does not demand completion.
Revisit the shelf every few months, not every day.
Let some ideas expire without turning it into a moral failure.

body.content: The work does not have to justify itself by becoming a product. Some of it is just practice. Some of it is compost. The shelf is not a backlog; it is a garden.
